title: [brc15a-pro-slider 10] Align CLI/docs with campaign mutation bounds
body:
<!-- repo-harness-campaign:v1
campaign_id=brc15a-20260907-pro-slider
group=1
slot=10
-->

Audit baseline: refs/heads/main at commit 33d692aaa0ab593df0c160082b18fdac02c82e9c.

```json
{
  "protocol": 1,
  "kind": "repo-harness-campaign-issue-metadata",
  "issue_kind": "bugfix",
  "primary_capability": "campaign-operator-guidance",
  "priority": "P3",
  "depends_on_slots": [
    "02",
    "06"
  ],
  "suspected_paths": [
    "README.md",
    "src/cli",
    "scripts"
  ]
}
```

Problem:
Operator-facing CLI output and documentation should consistently state the exact audit baseline, marker authority, allowed issue kinds, and forbidden mutations. If these constraints are scattered or implicit, future campaign runs can drift into title-based slot matching or broader GitHub mutations.

Repair:
Update the relevant CLI/help text and repository documentation to describe the campaign issue protocol as a bounded issue-author workflow: exact ref/SHA preflight, one issue per marker slot, one metadata fence, allowed issue kinds only, and no labels, milestones, assignees, code changes, PRs, or closures.

Acceptance:
- CLI/help text includes the audit-baseline requirement and forbidden mutation list.
- README or campaign docs state that the marker is the sole slot authority.
- Documentation examples include exactly one fenced JSON metadata object with the required keys.

Problem:
The operator web view needs regression coverage for empty groups, unreadable repositories, failed loads, and mixed success/error states. Without these fixtures, slider/worklist repairs can pass happy-path checks while breaking the states operators rely on during canary triage.

Repair:
Add UI-level fixtures or component tests that exercise all, unreadable, selected group, empty selected group, load failure, and mixed card/error populations. Assert both visible text and count semantics.

Acceptance:
- Empty and error states render actionable text without hiding navigation controls.
- Mixed readable/unreadable fixtures keep counts consistent with slot 01 semantics.
- Tests fail if a group selection displays stale cards from a previous group.

title: [brc15a-pro-slider 08] Validate depends_on_slots before emission
body:
<!-- repo-harness-campaign:v1
campaign_id=brc15a-20260907-pro-slider
group=1
slot=08
-->

Audit baseline: refs/heads/main at commit 33d692aaa0ab593df0c160082b18fdac02c82e9c.

```json
{
  "protocol": 1,
  "kind": "repo-harness-campaign-issue-metadata",
  "issue_kind": "bugfix",
  "primary_capability": "dependency-metadata",
  "priority": "P2",
  "depends_on_slots": [
    "05"
  ],
  "suspected_paths": [
    "src/core",
    "tests"
  ]
}
```

Problem:
depends_on_slots is part of the campaign metadata consumed by downstream planning. Without validation, a body can reference missing slots, malformed slot ids, or its own slot, causing the repair plan to appear ordered while actually being ambiguous.

Repair:
Validate depends_on_slots against the declared campaign slot set before issue body emission. Reject self-dependencies, duplicate dependencies, unknown slots, and non-zero-padded slot ids.

Acceptance:
- Valid prior-slot dependencies pass.
- Self, duplicate, unknown, and malformed dependencies fail with slot-specific diagnostics.
- The metadata emitted for all ten campaign slots remains valid after validation.

title: [brc15a-pro-slider 07] Add duplicate-slot and idempotency tests
body:
<!-- repo-harness-campaign:v1
campaign_id=brc15a-20260907-pro-slider
group=1
slot=07
-->

Audit baseline: refs/heads/main at commit 33d692aaa0ab593df0c160082b18fdac02c82e9c.

```json
{
  "protocol": 1,
  "kind": "repo-harness-campaign-issue-metadata",
  "issue_kind": "test_gap",
  "primary_capability": "slot-idempotency",
  "priority": "P2",
  "depends_on_slots": [
    "03",
    "04"
  ],
  "suspected_paths": [
    "tests",
    "src/core"
  ]
}
```

Problem:
The campaign requires exactly one issue for each slot. Tests should cover duplicate detection by body marker rather than title prefix, because the title prefix is display-only and may change without changing slot authority.

Repair:
Add idempotency tests for existing issue discovery, duplicate slot markers, title-only duplicates, and retry after partial failure. The test oracle should use campaign_id, group, and slot from the marker.

Acceptance:
- Existing issue with the same marker is treated as the slot record regardless of title text.
- Two bodies with the same marker fail duplicate-slot validation.
- Retrying after a failed slot does not create a second issue for a slot already observed created.

title: [brc15a-pro-slider 06] Strip forbidden issue mutation payload fields
body:
<!-- repo-harness-campaign:v1
campaign_id=brc15a-20260907-pro-slider
group=1
slot=06
-->

Audit baseline: refs/heads/main at commit 33d692aaa0ab593df0c160082b18fdac02c82e9c.

```json
{
  "protocol": 1,
  "kind": "repo-harness-campaign-issue-metadata",
  "issue_kind": "bugfix",
  "primary_capability": "bounded-issue-mutation",
  "priority": "P1",
  "depends_on_slots": [
    "04",
    "05"
  ],
  "suspected_paths": [
    "src/core",
    "src/cli",
    "tests"
  ]
}
```

Problem:
The bounded campaign permits creating the requested issues but forbids labels, milestones, assignees, branch changes, code changes, PRs, and closing issues. A reusable issue-author path should make forbidden mutation fields unrepresentable rather than relying on each caller to omit them.

Repair:
Introduce a narrow campaign issue payload type that only carries repository name, title, and body. Add an allowlist serialization step before the GitHub request so labels, assignees, milestone, state, and project fields cannot leak into the API call.

Acceptance:
- Fixtures containing labels, assignees, milestone, state, or project fields are rejected or stripped before write.
- The emitted GitHub create payload includes only title/body plus required repository routing.
- The action log confirms no forbidden mutation fields were sent.

title: [brc15a-pro-slider 05] Add metadata fence/schema validation tests
body:
<!-- repo-harness-campaign:v1
campaign_id=brc15a-20260907-pro-slider
group=1
slot=05
-->

Audit baseline: refs/heads/main at commit 33d692aaa0ab593df0c160082b18fdac02c82e9c.

```json
{
  "protocol": 1,
  "kind": "repo-harness-campaign-issue-metadata",
  "issue_kind": "test_gap",
  "primary_capability": "issue-metadata-validation",
  "priority": "P1",
  "depends_on_slots": [
    "03"
  ],
  "suspected_paths": [
    "tests",
    "src/core"
  ]
}
```

Problem:
Each campaign issue body must contain exactly one fenced JSON metadata object with a fixed protocol, kind, issue_kind, primary_capability, priority, depends_on_slots, and suspected_paths. Tests should prevent regressions that emit zero blocks, multiple blocks, non-JSON blocks, or unsupported issue kinds.

Repair:
Add schema-level fixtures for valid and invalid metadata blocks, including duplicate fences and additional required-key drift. Ensure only bugfix and test_gap are accepted issue_kind values.

Acceptance:
- Valid metadata with the required keys passes.
- Missing keys, extra fenced JSON blocks, malformed JSON, and unsupported issue_kind values fail.
- The validator reports the slot whose body failed validation.

title: [brc15a-pro-slider 04] Report per-slot GitHub write failures accurately
body:
<!-- repo-harness-campaign:v1
campaign_id=brc15a-20260907-pro-slider
group=1
slot=04
-->

Audit baseline: refs/heads/main at commit 33d692aaa0ab593df0c160082b18fdac02c82e9c.

```json
{
  "protocol": 1,
  "kind": "repo-harness-campaign-issue-metadata",
  "issue_kind": "bugfix",
  "primary_capability": "github-write-observation",
  "priority": "P1",
  "depends_on_slots": [],
  "suspected_paths": [
    "src/core",
    "src/cli",
    "tests"
  ]
}
```

Problem:
The campaign contract requires that success is claimed only for an issue that GitHub was observed to create or update. A batch author can otherwise report a slot as done after constructing the payload, even when the API call failed, timed out, or returned a non-issue response.

Repair:
Represent each slot with an explicit write state: not_attempted, attempted, observed_created, observed_updated, or failed. The final action log should be derived only from observed_created/observed_updated records.

Acceptance:
- Simulated API failure leaves the slot out of the success log and includes the failure reason.
- A response without issue number or URL is treated as failed.
- Partial batch success reports created slots and failed slots separately.

title: [brc15a-pro-slider 02] Enforce exact commit baseline before writes
body:
<!-- repo-harness-campaign:v1
campaign_id=brc15a-20260907-pro-slider
group=1
slot=02
-->

Audit baseline: refs/heads/main at commit 33d692aaa0ab593df0c160082b18fdac02c82e9c.

```json
{
  "protocol": 1,
  "kind": "repo-harness-campaign-issue-metadata",
  "issue_kind": "bugfix",
  "primary_capability": "baseline-preflight",
  "priority": "P1",
  "depends_on_slots": [],
  "suspected_paths": [
    "src/cli",
    "src/core",
    "tests"
  ]
}
```

Problem:
Campaign issue authorship depends on reading one exact ref/SHA pair and refusing writes when the observed branch head differs. If the preflight is only advisory or duplicated across paths, a later write step can accidentally act on a different revision than the audited baseline.

Repair:
Centralize the baseline preflight and require every write-capable campaign path to carry the verified ref and commit. Abort before issue creation when the requested ref, observed ref, or observed commit does not match.

Acceptance:
- A SHA mismatch fixture exits before any GitHub write payload is constructed.
- The failure message names the requested ref, requested commit, observed ref, and observed commit.
- Happy-path issue creation still records the exact audit baseline in the body.


Problem:
The operator worklist should keep task-card totals, unreadable repository rows, and active group/filter counts distinct. The current UI behavior is susceptible to showing inconsistent totals when unreadable repositories and named groups are present, making the slider/worklist audit view hard to trust.

Repair:
Normalize the count source used by the group chips, selected group title, and visible empty state. Ensure unreadable repositories are counted only in the control that explicitly represents them.

Acceptance:
- Mixed task-card and unreadable-repository fixture renders stable, non-duplicated counts.
- Switching between all, unreadable, and a named group does not change total semantics.
- Regression coverage captures the mixed-population case.
